citations.short: Procedures not  in writing, fully followed
citations.long: The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing.

citations.short: Buildings not maintained in good state of repair
citations.long: Buildings used in the manufacturing, processing, packing, and holding of a drug product are not maintained in a good state of repair.
Equipment and utensils are not cleaned at appropriate intervals to prevent contamination that would alter the safety, identity, strength, quality or purity of the drug product.

citations.short: Computer control of master formula records
citations.long: Appropriate controls are not exercised over computers or related systems to assure that changes in master production and control records or other records are instituted only by authorized personnel.

There are no written procedures for production and process controls designed to assure that the drug products have the identity, strength, quality, and purity they purport or are represented to possess.
Determinations of conformance to appropriate written specifications for acceptance are not made for drug products.

citations.short: Instruments, apparatus, et. al. not meeting specs
citations.long: The use of instruments not meeting established specifications was observed.
The accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and reproducibility of test methods have not been established.
There is a failure to thoroughly review any unexplained discrepancy whether or not the batch has been already distributed.
Procedures describing the handling of written and oral complaints related to drug products are deficiently written or followed.
The quality control unit lacks the responsibility and authority to reject all drug products.

citations.short: Authority lacking to review records, investigate errors
citations.long: The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
Adequate lab facilities for testing and approval or rejection of components and drug product containers are not available to the quality control unit.

citations.short: Procedures not  in writing, fully followed
citations.long: The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing.

citations.short: Adequate space lacking  to prevent mix-ups and contamination
citations.long: The building lacks adequate space for the orderly placement of equipment and materials to prevent mix-ups between different components, in-process materials, and drug products and to prevent contamination.
Drains are not provided with an air break or other mechanical device to prevent back-siphonage where connected directly with a sewer.

citations.short: Computer control of master formula records
citations.long: Appropriate controls are not exercised over computers or related systems to assure that changes in master production and control records or other records are instituted only by authorized personnel.

citations.short: In process materials - conformance to written specs
citations.long: Laboratory controls do not include a determination of conformance to written specifications for in-process materials.
Reserve drug product samples are not retained and stored under conditions consistent with product labeling.

citations.short: Complete instructions, procedures, specifications et. al.
citations.long: Master production and control records lack complete manufacturing and control instructions.
Procedures describing the handling of written and oral complaints related to drug products are deficiently written or followed.

citations.short: Authority lacking to review records, investigate errors
citations.long: The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.

citations.short: Procedures not  in writing, fully followed
citations.long: The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing.
Employees engaged in the manufacture of a drug product lack the training required to perform their assigned functions.

Individuals responsible for supervising the manufacture, processing, packing, and holding of a drug product lack the training to perform their assigned functions in such a manner as to assure the drug product has the safety, identity, strength, quality and purity that it purports or is represented to possess.
Routine calibration of mechanical equipment is not performed according to a written program designed to assure proper performance.

citations.short: Backup data not assured as exact and complete
citations.long: Backup data is not assured as exact and secure from alteration, erasure or loss through keeping hard copy or alternate systems.

citations.short: Establish reliability of supplier's C of A
citations.long: Establishment of the reliability of the component supplier's report of analyses is deficient in that the test results are not appropriately validated at appropriate intervals.

Laboratory controls do not include the establishment of scientifically sound and appropriate test procedures designed to assure that in-process materials conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality and purity.

Testing and release of drug product for distribution do not include appropriate laboratory determination of satisfactory conformance to the final specifications and identity and strength of each active ingredient prior to release.

citations.short: Annual visual exams of drug products
citations.long: Reserve samples from representative sample lots or batches of drug products selected by acceptable statistical procedures are not examined visually at least once a year for evidence of deterioration.
Laboratory records are deficient in that they do not include a complete record of all data obtained during testing.
